properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): every typed edge helper's served description says "MANY AT ONCE: `draw_edges`, items {"tool": …}", and an agent sent `items`, which draw_edges refuses (it takes `edges`). The wording has been there since #629 (2026-09-29); the field was `edges` from the start. A RECURRENCE of the 2026-09-28 class: argument names written in served text are checked against no schema
properties.statement:
① OBSERVED: Shop session 6 (2026-10-26, flo2.io, reflow2 0.92.0). The agent reported "The description of the `invalidates` tool says the batch tool `draw_edges` takes `items`; it actually takes `edges`."

The text is generated in crates/reflow2-mcp/src/bulk_edges.rs:107 (name_the_bulk_route), on main 5d34529f0:
"{base} MANY AT ONCE: `draw_edges`, items {"tool": "<name>", "arguments": {…}}, same checks, all or nothing."
DrawEdgesReq (bulk_edges.rs:150) takes `edges: Vec<DrawEdgeItem>`, with deny_unknown_fields.

NOT AFFECTED: draw_edges' own description and schema, and the refusal (which names the field path).

② PRECEDENT: fact:root-cause-instructions-route-records-to-paths-that-cannot-take-them-and-the-lint-checks-names-only-2026-09-28. That finding names this class and proposed a pinning test: "(2) every `tool`'s `param` pair and '`tool` takes `param`' sentence in a skill resolves against that tool's toolsnap input schema". That test was never written.

③ CANDIDATES:
(a) The generated sentence uses "items" as plain English for the list's elements, in the place where an argument name reads.
(b) draw_edges' field was renamed after the text was written.
(c) flo2's door rewrote the description.
(d) The agent misread the text.

④⑤ MEASURED:
- (b) REFUTED. `git log -S` shows the sentence and the `edges` field both arrive in 083790ec9 (#629, 2026-09-29), so the field was never `items`.
- (c) REFUTED. The text is reflow2's own, and flo2 forwards reflow2's descriptions unchanged.
- (d) REFUTED. The text does read "`draw_edges`, items {…}", and an agent that took it at its word was refused.
- (a) HOLDS. It reaches every helper in HELPERS (the typed edge tools, ~32).

⑥ CLASS: argument names that served text writes by hand (tool descriptions, generated suffixes, skills) are checked against no input schema. skill_lint checks tool NAMES only. Fixing the class (pinning test (2) of 2026-09-28, extended to served descriptions) would have failed #629 on the day it merged, and it would have caught this. The instance fix alone is one word ("`edges` [{…}]").

⑦ PINNING TEST, not written: every backticked `tool` followed by an argument or object key in a served description or skill resolves against that tool's input schema. This text fails it today.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: how many other descriptions name arguments that do not exist. No census was run.
